newsitem.title: USA: Techne backs FY '97 net of $1.10 a share.
newsitem.headline: Techne backs FY '97 net of $1.10 a share.

text.p: Techne Corp, which makes products for the clinical diagnostics market, on Friday backed analysts' estimates for fiscal 1997 earnings of $1.10 a share.

"I think it ($1.10) is attainable," said Chief Executive Officer Thomas Oland. "I can't guarantee we'll do it, but if we do the revenues I expect, I don't think it'll be a problem," Oland said after Techne's annual meeting here.
Techne earned $0.89 a share for its fiscal year ended June 30, 1996. Yesterday, the company reported earnings for its fiscal 1997 first quarter ended September 30 of $0.22 a share.

Oland predicted sales of Techne's biotechnology products would increase at least 15 percent in fiscal 1997. "In biotechnology, market growth is good, and our volumes are up, but we're seeing more competition," he said. "Consequently, we're giving up a little more in discounts. That's why our strategy has to be to make that next jump in technology."

Last year, Techne's biotechnology products sales grew 17 percent to $43.6 million, accounting for 80 percent of the company's total sales. In the first quarter this year, biotechnology sales also increased 17 percent to $11.6 million and pre-tax earnings increased 28 percent to $2.9 million.
Oland predicted sales of Techne's hematology products would rise four to five percent in fiscal 1997.
"I expect hematology's natural growth rate of four to five percent in sales to continue," Oland said.
Last year, Techne's hematology products sales grew 5.8 percent to $11.0 million, accounting for 20 percent of the company's total sales.
Oland said research and development costs should not exceed 20 percent of revenues in fiscal 1997.
"I'd like to hold it (R&D as a proportion of sales) at no more than 20 percent," Oland said.
Techne's R&D spending as a percent of revenues has increased from 18 percent in fiscal 1995 to 19 percent in fiscal 1996, to 21 percent in the first quarter of fiscal 1997.
